You don’t have to trust photos from space to check the Earth’s shape. People worked out that it was round long before cameras or satellites existed.

One thing you can observe yourself is that the stars change as you travel north or south. In the Northern Hemisphere, Polaris gets lower in the sky as you head toward the equator, then disappears below the horizon farther south. A spherical Earth explains that pattern, along with time zones and the different noon shadow angles measured in different places.

What convinced you the Earth is flat, and what kind of evidence would make you reconsider?

3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s a mixture of colors. When it enters Earth’s atmosphere, it runs into tiny molecules of air. Those molecules scatter some of the light, sending it off in different directions.

Here’s the important part: they scatter short wavelengths, such as blue, much more strongly than long wavelengths, such as red. So when you look at the sky away from the Sun, plenty of scattered blue light reaches your eyes.

You might wonder why the sky isn’t violet, since violet has an even shorter wavelength. Sunlight contains less violet than blue, and our eyes are much less sensitive to violet.

At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere before reaching you. Much of the blue gets scattered out of that direct path, leaving the warmer reds and oranges.

雨从入夜起便没有停。路灯下，细密的雨丝斜斜落着，把空荡的街道织成一条发亮的河。末班公交驶过，轮胎推开积水，声音很快消失在巷口。窗内的台灯亮着，杯中的茶已经凉了。有人收起湿伞，在楼道里轻轻跺脚，接着传来钥匙碰撞的脆响。我把窗关小一些，仍留一道缝，听雨点敲着铁皮雨棚。远处一扇窗忽然熄了灯，夜便又深了一点。
